blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (Path traversal in read_attachment through the client-supplied name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Validate `name` where it enters (CWE-22): reject it unless it equals `os.path.basename(name)` and is not empty, `.` or `..`, or better look it up in the `attachments` table for this `ticket_id` and open only a stored name; then check that the resolved path (`os.path.realpath`) stays under `UPLOAD_DIR/<ticket_id>`. The `may_read_ticket` check on line 28 only covers `ticket_id`, so without this fix it protects nothing. Add a test that `read_attachment` refuses `../2/x.png`, `../../../../etc/passwd` and `/etc/passwd`.
findings.title: Path traversal in read_attachment through the client-supplied name

findings.recommendation: Give `save_attachment` the caller's identity and check on the server that it may write to `ticket_id` (CWE-862), as `read_attachment` does with `may_read_ticket`; otherwise any caller of the upload entry point attaches files to any ticket. Confidence low: the HTTP handler calling it is not in the change, so whether it checks ownership could not be verified.
findings.title: save_attachment takes no caller and checks no authorization

findings.evidence:
with open(os.path.join(directory, name), "wb") as f:
    f.write(data)
_conn.execute(
    "INSERT INTO attachments (ticket_id, name, size) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
findings.recommendation: Store each upload under a server-generated name (a UUID, or the row id) and keep the client's filename only as display metadata, or refuse an existing name (open with mode `"xb"`). As written, whoever can upload to a ticket replaces a file agents already trust — e.g. a screenshot swapped for a malicious document under the same name — and the table keeps two rows pointing at one file with a stale `size`. Confidence low: who may upload to a ticket depends on the caller, not visible in the change.
findings.title: An upload silently overwrites an earlier attachment of the same name
